transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-09-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Recording: Fireflies.ai auto
Attendees: Sarah Lin (AE, Redwood); Marco Diaz (SE, Redwood); Priya Nair (CSM, Redwood); Laura Kent (CISO, Bridgewater); Mike Owens (CTO, Bridgewater); Jenna Park (PM, Bridgewater); Tom Reyes (Infra)

Summary (auto): Bridgewater Trust evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PII/financial workloads. Primary concerns: data residency (EU/US separation), logging restrictions, audit logs retention, KMS/HSM, SSO, SOC2/ISO compliance. Next steps agreed: send security pack, schedule deep dive, pilot pricing.

[00:00] Sarah Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate ya. I'm Sarah from Redwood, AE on this account, with Marco our SE. Quick intros?
[00:23] Laura Kent: Hi all, Laura here, CISO at Bridgewater. We're leading compliance review - GDPR, bank regs, logging constraints.
[00:30] Mike Owens: Mike, CTO. Primary for me is latency and how this would fit into our private cloud strategy.
[00:38] Jenna Park: Jenna, product, mostly curious about timeline and cost.
[00:42] Tom Reyes: Tom, infra. I'll be working with Marco on network details and VPC peering.
[00:48] Marco Diaz: Thanks - Marco here. We'll cover architecture options: Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, Private control plane, and what each buys you on data residency and logging.

[01:12] Sarah Lin: To set context, are you leaning toward an on-prem private deployment or are you open to Redwood Dedicated in a customer-dedicated VPC?
[01:25] Laura Kent: Ideally we'd keep EU customer data in EU-only infrastructure; for US accounts US-only. Also on logging: we cannot have full request logs retained by vendor beyond 30 days, and certain sensitive fields must be redacted or never logged.
[01:40] Mike Owens: Right - and performance wise we need sub-200ms tail latency on short requests for some use cases. If we go private, we need to understand tradeoffs vs hosted.

[02:05] Marco Diaz: Totally. High level: Redwood Hosted is fastest to go live, but data centers are in shared infra - we do offer region pinning though. Redwood Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and VPC peering, plus config to limit logs and optional private control plane. Redwood Private is full customer-managed control plane or on-prem - that gives you strict data residency and full control over logging and retention.
[02:35] Laura Kent: What's the difference between dedicated and private control plane? In terms of audit logs and access?
[02:45] Marco Diaz: With Dedicated, control plane is still Redwood-managed but with tenant isolation and dedicated capacity; we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding and support limiting retention. Private gives you the control plane endpoints in your VPC - your network controls access, and Redwood's control plane components can be deployed in your cloud or on-prem. So audit logs are under your retention policy.

[03:20] Jenna Park: A few practical Qs: does Redwood support SSO (SAML/Okta) and RBAC for model access and who can call the API?
[03:29] Priya Nair: Yes - we integrate with SAML/Okta, SCIM for provisioning, and per-route RBAC. You can create roles that restrict who can call generation endpoints vs who can see logs.
[03:40] Laura Kent: Good. KMS/HSM integration? We cannot allow vendor-managed keys for some datasets.
[03:46] Marco Diaz: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM workflows for on-prem. For Private we can wire your HSM directly - so keys never leave your boundary.

[04:10] Tom Reyes: Network wise - we need VPC peering or PrivateLink. Does Dedicated support PrivateLink?
[04:18] Marco Diaz: Yes we support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on region - Private deployments obviously sit inside your VPC. For Dedicated we provision dedicated GPU clusters in your region and peer them into your network.

[04:39] Mike Owens: About logs - you mentioned forwarding to our SIEM. Can we also redact PII at the edge before any pencil of request leaves our network?
[04:48] Marco Diaz: For Private deployments yes, you can run pre-processing to redact fields. For Dedicated/Hosted we have request-redaction options and policy-based field masking; note that the masking happens in runtime so we recommend Private if you need absolute guarantee that raw data never leaves your network.

[05:20] Laura Kent: Audit wise we need immutable logs for certain ops and evidence for regulators. Can Redwood provide tamper-evident audit trails?
[05:29] Marco Diaz: We offer append-only audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM; for Private you can ship logs to a write-once store under your control. For Dedicated we can provide signed log exports. We'll put details in the security pack.

[06:02] Jenna Park: Any certs? SOC 2, ISO?
[06:06] Sarah Lin: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001 artifacts; we also have whitepapers for data residency and KMS/HSM. We'll attach the artifacts.

[06:25] Laura Kent: What about GDPR data subject requests - e.g., right to be forgotten? If logs contain user prompts, how do we handle deletion?
[06:34] Marco Diaz: We can configure retention policies per-customer so logs older than X days are auto-purged. For Hosted, we support deletion by request; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and deletion. Also we support redaction at ingestion for PII to reduce need to delete later.

[07:05] Mike Owens: Performance: if we run a dedicated pool in EU, what kind of throughput and latency can we expect for our 2k qps peak?
[07:16] Marco Diaz: High-level, depends on model size and batching. I'll run a tuned estimate post-call - e.g., for 7B-ish models we can target ~50ms p95 token latency with continuous batching; for larger models latencies scale up. I'll include a spreadsheet.

[07:50] Sarah Lin: Is anyone already running production ML infra on cloud regions they manage? We ask to see current infra to scope integration.
[07:58] Tom Reyes: We have GCP in EU-west and AWS in us-east; currently some ML workloads on premise for sensitive processing.

[08:15] Marco Diaz: Good - that helps. For billing and compliance: Dedicated is usually our go-to for banks - predictable throughput and SLA; Private if legal requires on-prem or fully isolated control plane.

[08:45] Laura Kent: A specific ask: we cannot have raw prompts retained beyond 30 days in vendor logs, and certain types of logs can't include account numbers or other PAN fields. Can that be enforced?
[08:57] Marco Diaz: Yes - we can set a 30-day retention on vendor-side logs, and implement field-level masking to strip PAN fields. For extra assurance we recommend Private so your preprocessors can redact before it hits the model or vendor logs.

[09:20] Jenna Park: How long to pilot / POC? We'd ideally run a 6-week pilot and then decide Q4.
[09:29] Sarah Lin: That's workable. Typical pilot is 4-8 weeks: initial integration, run benchmarks, measure QA/regression. We'll support with SE time and a playbook.

[10:00] Mike Owens: Any red flags on legal side? Our procurement will want to see indemnity and data residency clauses.
[10:07] Sarah Lin: We have standard language and enterprise addendum for higher assurances. We'll share a redline-friendly legal pack.

[10:22] Laura Kent: Do you support HIPAA? We have some B2B products ingesting health-related claims occasionally.
[10:29] Sarah Lin: Yes, we support HIPAA-compliant deployments under a Business Associate Agreement and can sign a BAA for Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted can be evaluated but typically customers requiring HIPAA prefer Dedicated or Private.

[10:55] Marco Diaz: Quick note on model variants - we support running quantized variants for cost/perf tradeoffs; that's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations. For sensitive workloads we recommend model and quantization profiles that avoid sending extra telemetry.

[11:20] Tom Reyes: On telemetry - what exactly does Redwood log by default? Full prompts, model outputs, token-level traces?
[11:28] Marco Diaz: Default: request metadata, prompts, responses, basic runtime telemetry. But we have opt-out and redaction controls. For Dedicated we can disable prompt logging entirely and send only aggregated telemetry. For Private you control telemetry completely.

[12:03] Laura Kent: Can you support legal-wanted audit for who invoked which model and when, without exposing full prompts?
[12:10] Marco Diaz: Yes - per-call metadata (user ID, route, timestamp) can be kept with masked or omitted prompt text. That satisfies many audit requirements.

[12:40] Jenna Park: Let's talk cost qualitatively - what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated/Private?
[12:47] Sarah Lin: Hosted is typically lowest up-front; Dedicated has a reservation/commit component for predictable throughput and better unit economics; Private has higher setup and OPEX for on-prem but gives full control. We'll share tiered pricing and examples in the follow-up.

[13:15] Mike Owens: Any SLAs for latency?
[13:18] Marco Diaz: We provide SLOs and can offer SLA-backed latency targets on Dedicated with certain configs and committed capacity. We'll include the SLA numbers in the pack.

[13:40] Laura Kent: Data residency - can we ensure EU data never leaves EU for backups, logs, and failover?
[13:48] Marco Diaz: Yes. We partition storage and backups by region and can prevent cross-border replication. For failover we can configure same-region failover; cross-region only with explicit permission.

[14:10] Tom Reyes: Network ingress/egress - does Redwood support IP allowlists and mutual TLS?
[14:17] Marco Diaz: Yes - mutual TLS, IP allowlists, and private connectivity for Dedicated. For Private we sit behind your network controls.

[14:40] Jenna Park: From a product perspective, if we start with Dedicated, how hard is it to migrate to Private later?
[14:47] Marco Diaz: Migration path is supported - same APIs and routes; migration is mostly control-plane and network. We'll help create a migration plan if you decide to move from Dedicated to Private.

[15:05] Laura Kent: On encryption at rest: keys per-tenant?
[15:10] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support per-tenant encryption keys and customer-managed keys via KMS; for Private you can use your HSM.

[15:30] Mike Owens: Are there any regulatory reports or assessments you can provide specific to banks?
[15:36] Sarah Lin: We have compliance packs and can provide references and prior bank case studies under NDA. We'll include a short one pager.

[16:00] Marco Diaz: I'll flag two technical items for the deep dive: benchmark with their 2k qps profile and verify VPC peering options in eu-west + us-east.

[16:20] Tom Reyes: Noted. I'll share an infra diagram after the call.

[16:30] Laura Kent: A question on retention contracts: if we sign annual for dedicated capacity, can we change retention policies mid-contract?
[16:38] Sarah Lin: Retention is a configuration; we'd work through change control and SLAs. For policy changes that impact billing or storage we may need a formal change request.

[17:00] Jenna Park: Anything from a risk perspective we haven't covered?
[17:05] Laura Kent: I want assurance on pen testing and vulnerability scanning cadence.

[17:10] Marco Diaz: We run quarterly pentests and regular vulnerability scans; results and remediation timelines can be shared under NDA.

[17:30] Sarah Lin: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, security pack incl KMS/HSM notes, sample SLA and pricing, Marco will do perf estimate, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive for next Wed.

[17:45] Mike Owens: Works for me.

[17:49] Laura Kent: Works. Please include legal pack so procurement can start redline.

[17:53] Sarah Lin: Will do. Thanks everyone.

[18:05] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript has occasional ASR mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache) and filler words preserved. Shared artifacts mentioned: security-pack.pdf (to be sent), perf-spreadsheet.xlsx (Marco to produce), legal-addendum.docx.
